name: nlp_dpo_preference_bad
title: Hand-rolled direct preference optimisation whose reference model keeps its graph, whose evaluation runs in train mode, and whose sampling pass generates with gradients on
origin: hardening round 2, domain-nlp, 2026-09-14 - LLM post-training (DPO / RLHF), a shape the corpus had no example of in any family
note: This program carries a FORBIDDEN label that fires today. MLV501 reports at medium / confidence 0.900 (certain) that `chosen, rejected ... are never moved before pair()` about line 58, which reads `loss = pair(move(chosen, device), move(rejected, device))` - and move() is a workspace function whose entire body is a .to(device) comprehension. Spelling the same move as an inline dict comprehension, or rebinding chosen/rejected first, does not help. See NLP2-02 for the minimal repro; the gate is red on this program on purpose until that is fixed.

expected.defect: evaluate() never calls policy.eval(); only the reference model is put in eval mode, on line 94
expected.why: the policy is a decoder-only LM with dropout in every block, so the preference accuracy printed after each epoch is measured through a randomly thinned network

expected.defect: evaluate() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad() and carries no decorator
expected.why: two full LM forwards per batch keep their graphs alive for the whole evaluation, which on a 0.5B model is the difference between fitting in memory and not

expected.defect: sample_completions() calls policy.generate() with gradients on and the policy still in train mode
expected.why: generation with an autograd graph over max_new_tokens=128 steps is a guaranteed out-of-memory on any real model, and dropout during sampling makes the qualitative examples unrepresentative
the preference pairs come back in a different order each epoch, so no pair-by-pair comparison between epochs is possible

expected.defect: get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup is stepped once per call to train_epoch - that is once per epoch - instead of once per optimizer step
expected.why: the cosine schedule is built for len(train_loader) * epochs steps and receives one, so the learning rate never leaves warmup

expected.defect: the device is hard-coded to cuda with no availability check
expected.why: the script cannot be smoke-tested on a CPU box

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or python random
expected.why: DPO on preference data is noisy enough that two unseeded runs at lr=5e-7 disagree about which checkpoint is better

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled instead of policy.state_dict()
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path and cannot be loaded without the exact transformers version that wrote it

forbidden.why: every batch is moved before the forward: line 58 is `pair(move(chosen, device), move(rejected, device))` and move() (line 50) is `{key: value.to(device) for key, value in batch.items()}`. MLV501's own evidence line - 'no .to()/.cuda() on the batch, in the Dataset.__getitem__, or in a collate_fn' - is false about this file
optimizer.zero_grad() is called on line 61; it is after step(), which is legal and is the pattern the HuggingFace examples use
there is no torch.no_grad() block anywhere in this project - that absence is MLV302's finding
neither DataLoader takes num_workers=, and main() is reachable only from the __main__ guard (line 113)
there is no CrossEntropyLoss in this project; the DPO objective is -logsigmoid of a margin and torch.log_softmax on line 37 is the log-probability the objective is defined over
F.logsigmoid is the DPO loss itself, not a sigmoid feeding a BCE loss - no BCELoss or BCEWithLogitsLoss is constructed anywhere
the policy and the reference are assigned directly to attributes (lines 18-19); no plain list or dict of modules exists
no sklearn transformer is fitted anywhere in this project
load_pairs reads a dataset that is already split into train and test; no split call exists here
preference_accuracy compares two log-probability scalars with > (line 51), which is a comparison, not a metric fed logits
there is no HuggingFace Trainer here - the loop is hand-written

unsupported.defect: the reference forward is not wrapped in torch.no_grad() and the reference's parameters are only frozen in main(); the reference branch of every batch still builds a graph
unsupported.why: the reference forward is inside a training step, so MLV302's eval-region shape does not cover it and no rule models a frozen model whose gradients are still computed

unsupported.defect: the epoch loss accumulates the tensor rather than loss.item(), so every batch's two-model graph stays alive for the epoch
unsupported.why: MLV205 models exactly this, but it cannot type a loss produced by a workspace nn.Module - see NLP2-09; recorded here as unsupported rather than expected so the same hole is not counted twice

unsupported.defect: none - the mean() is present, which is what makes the objective a scalar
unsupported.why: MLV212 is a later-tier rule and is not built
